title: My game, Sunday Fighter Pilot, was made 100% with AI and is now out on Steam
author: ledniv
selftext:
**Sunday Fighter Pilot** is out on Steam! Made 100% with AI using a combination of Astra and Opus 5.5.

It’s a flying sandbox where you can explore, discover airfields and unlock planes. Fly around and enjoy the scenery, try flying through barns and under bridges, or use guns and rockets to blow stuff up and capture territory.

It did very well during Steam Next Fest, so I added a ton more content for the release. Nearly doubled the content in the game in roughly a week.

[Sunday Fighter Pilot on Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5074480/Sunday_Fighter_Pilot/)

The game started in Three.js with an Electron wrapper, then was ported to native Rust using wgpu. During the port, the original game was used to check that the flight model and gameplay still behaved the same.

I had both models follow my [data oriented design skill](https://github.com/Data-Oriented-Design-for-Games/data-oriented-design).. It gives the AI concrete instructions for structuring the game around data and the functions that update it. In this project, that means parallel arrays, pooled memory and flight simulation kept separate from rendering. Keeping the data and logic explicit makes it easier to see what a feature changes and how it fits into the existing code.

The AI also built development tools, including terrain and vegetation generators, 3D model viewers, and an interactive map for inspecting the whole world. Automated gameplay captures and regression tests were used to check changes, including making sure the world generates consistently across Windows, Mac and Linux.

Happy to answer questions about the game or how I made it.

comments.author: Bloobat
comments.body: Why charge for it? Ai game projects can be cool and fun but charging real money for them just feels plain wrong.

replies.author: Bloobat
replies.body: Also I will add this does look like fun I was just disappointed to click through and see it has a price tag

replies.author: Confident-Log1321
replies.body: I think for 10 bucks we can do better than colorful polygons and blocks with less fidelity than Minecraft lol

replies.author: Lattarde
replies.body: So you sell a game that no ones play? [https://steamdb.info/app/5074480/charts/](https://steamdb.info/app/5074480/charts/)

replies.author: Bloobat
replies.body:
And? There's plenty of absolute garbage games no even made with ai that also 'sell copies'... You'd need to sell atleast a 1000 copies to make any serious money and that's besides the point.... The point is there's the fun side of ai game dev which is cool new projects from people using ai to unlock their abilities, and then there's the bad side of ai game dev which is people to pushing out AI slop as quick as possible to try make a quick buck. It's literally embarrassing. 

Now if you had overheads, servers to maintain etc then absolutely fair play.

replies.body: Yeah, I also develop programs using AI, and I think its just a great hobby, but I dont think its right to make money off of it, I only release everything as open source.

comments.author: Undumed
comments.body: Damn, $10 for a game made in a month using AI with a total cost of $100

comments.author: wylderzone
comments.body:
Came here to say the same thing. One of the biggest problems with AI made games right now, isn't that it is made with AI. It is the fact that the people making it are utterly detached from reality in terms of what their game  offers for the money they are asking for.

You can literally buy one of, if not the best, flight games - IL-2 Sturmovik for less than what you are charging right now.

People currently cranking out games with AI have little to no understanding of the market. You said it did well during Nextfest - it peaked at 6 players ...

  
Also you've put out a game a month it seems. Serious question - what are you hoping to achieve? Why not do one thing well ?

replies.body:
It’s all flash. It’s like all those guys when ai video came out they released a 1 minute trailer for their new TV SERIES. Notice those aren’t around. It’s the same mentality. AI is a great tool but these guys think it lets you compete at a higher level.

No one is buying this game for $10z

comments.body: Until the majority of people who are sitting pretty holding up the consumption racket we live in are content to accept that there is no active and current prosecution of the intellectual property copyright infringements absolutely necessary for mainstream commercial ai models to succeed as commercial products: thank you for being up front and honest about this, you're out to make $10 on a $100 fee and however many hours of work

comments.author: gabro-games
comments.body: Looks nice! I like the low poly art style. UI needs some love and probably needs a bit more direction in terms of gameplay (challenges etc.) but it's promising. Best of luck with it.

comments.author: Sad_Library123
comments.body:
I have recently started The Iconoclasts Spotlight, a substack spotlighting new games by indie devs.

I won’t exclude the game if they include AI but the problem is see again and again is that the people making these games have no eye for quality, broader game design, storytelling and direction.

I spend the last decade in graphic design, traditional art, and asset designs, if you can’t critique yourself, that’s problem.

Second opinion ≠ Validation

Stop jumping to validation and look deeply at what your making.
